COMPOUND WRITING: HOW I TURNED MY PROCESS INTO A PLUGIN https://every.


I’VE PACKAGED MY METHODS FOR INTERVIEWING, OUTLINING, DRAFTING, AND REVISING INTO REUSABLE AI SKILLS. HERE’S HOW TO PUT THEM TO WORK. https://every.

by Katie Parrott https://every.to/emails/click/1eb47536f45a3508ca723b5b2cb780e942839f966e324ef3162cd49469aec49f/eyJzdWJqZWN0IjoiQ29tcG91bmQgV3JpdGluZzogSG93IEkgVHVybmVkIE15IFByb2Nlc3MgSW50byBhIFBsdWdpbiIsInBvc3RfaWQiOjQ0NjIsInBvc3RfdHlwZSI6InBvc3QiLCJ1cmwiOiJodHRwczovL2V2ZXJ5LnRvL0BrYXRpZS5wYXJyb3R0MTIiLCJwb3NpdGlvbiI6NH0=

https://every.to/emails/click/1eb47536f45a3508ca723b5b2cb780e942839f966e324ef3162cd49469aec49f/eyJzdWJqZWN0IjoiQ29tcG91bmQgV3JpdGluZzogSG93IEkgVHVybmVkIE15IFByb2Nlc3MgSW50byBhIFBsdWdpbiIsInBvc3RfaWQiOjQ0NjIsInBvc3RfdHlwZSI6InBvc3QiLCJ1cmwiOiJodHRwczovL3lvdXR1LmJlL3ZleV9kQm5EVEFVIiwicG9zaXRpb24iOjV9

The usual question about AI writing is “Did a human write this, or did AI?” We think that’s the wrong frame. Writing is a process of thinking, developing ideas, drafting, editing, and publishing. AI can help throughout, but AI doesn’t write. People write with AI, well or poorly.

At Every, we’ve explored this for years. Dan Shipper https://every.to/emails/click/1eb47536f45a3508ca723b5b2cb780e942839f966e324ef3162cd49469aec49f/eyJzdWJqZWN0IjoiQ29tcG91bmQgV3JpdGluZzogSG93IEkgVHVybmVkIE15IFByb2Nlc3MgSW50byBhIFBsdWdpbiIsInBvc3RfaWQiOjQ0NjIsInBvc3RfdHlwZSI6InBvc3QiLCJ1cmwiOiJodHRwczovL2V2ZXJ5LnRvL0BkYW5zaGlwcGVyIiwicG9zaXRpb24iOjZ9 wrote an early guide to writing essays with AI, Katie Parrott https://every.to/emails/click/1eb47536f45a3508ca723b5b2cb780e942839f966e324ef3162cd49469aec49f/eyJzdWJqZWN0IjoiQ29tcG91bmQgV3JpdGluZzogSG93IEkgVHVybmVkIE15IFByb2Nlc3MgSW50byBhIFBsdWdpbiIsInBvc3RfaWQiOjQ0NjIsInBvc3RfdHlwZSI6InBvc3QiLCJ1cmwiOiJodHRwczovL2V2ZXJ5LnRvL0BrYXRpZS5wYXJyb3R0MTIiLCJwb3NpdGlvbiI6N30= has documented her process in Working Overtime https://every.to/emails/click/1eb47536f45a3508ca723b5b2cb780e942839f966e324ef3162cd49469aec49f/eyJzdWJqZWN0IjoiQ29tcG91bmQgV3JpdGluZzogSG93IEkgVHVybmVkIE15IFByb2Nlc3MgSW50byBhIFBsdWdpbiIsInBvc3RfaWQiOjQ0NjIsInBvc3RfdHlwZSI6InBvc3QiLCJ1cmwiOiJodHRwczovL2V2ZXJ5LnRvL3dvcmtpbmctb3ZlcnRpbWUiLCJwb3NpdGlvbiI6OH0=, and Laura Entis https://every.to/emails/click/1eb47536f45a3508ca723b5b2cb780e942839f966e324ef3162cd49469aec49f/eyJzdWJqZWN0IjoiQ29tcG91bmQgV3JpdGluZzogSG93IEkgVHVybmVkIE15IFByb2Nlc3MgSW50byBhIFBsdWdpbiIsInBvc3RfaWQiOjQ0NjIsInBvc3RfdHlwZSI6InBvc3QiLCJ1cmwiOiJodHRwczovL2V2ZXJ5LnRvL0BsYXVyYV8yN2JiYWZfMSIsInBvc2l0aW9uIjo5fQ== recently argued in defense of the practice https://every.. We’ve also shared how our editorial team uses AI https://every. and published guidelines https://every. requiring human authors to stand behind every piece.

How We Write Now is a series about those processes. We’re starting with Compound Writing, a plugin and guide Katie has spent six months building and using. Inspired by Kieran Klaassen’s Compound Engineering https://every. and Dan’s agent-native architectures https://every.to/emails/click/1eb47536f45a3508ca723b5b2cb780e942839f966e324ef3162cd49469aec49f/eyJzdWJqZWN0IjoiQ29tcG91bmQgV3JpdGluZzogSG93IEkgVHVybmVkIE15IFByb2Nlc3MgSW50byBhIFBsdWdpbiIsInBvc3RfaWQiOjQ0NjIsInBvc3RfdHlwZSI6InBvc3QiLCJ1cmwiOiJodHRwczovL2V2ZXJ5LnRvL2d1aWRlcy9hZ2VudC1uYXRpdmUiLCJwb3NpdGlvbiI6MTR9, it provides reusable skills for developing ideas, shaping drafts, reviewing work, and carrying what you learn into the next piece—all around your voice and standards. Katie also joined Natalia Quintero https://every.to/emails/click/1eb47536f45a3508ca723b5b2cb780e942839f966e324ef3162cd49469aec49f/eyJzdWJqZWN0IjoiQ29tcG91bmQgV3JpdGluZzogSG93IEkgVHVybmVkIE15IFByb2Nlc3MgSW50byBhIFBsdWdpbiIsInBvc3RfaWQiOjQ0NjIsInBvc3RfdHlwZSI6InBvc3QiLCJ1cmwiOiJodHRwczovL2V2ZXJ5LnRvL0BuYXRhbGlhXzI5NDQiLCJwb3NpdGlvbiI6MTV9, Every’s head of consulting, on AI & I https://every.to/emails/click/1eb47536f45a3508ca723b5b2cb780e942839f966e324ef3162cd49469aec49f/eyJzdWJqZWN0IjoiQ29tcG91bmQgV3JpdGluZzogSG93IEkgVHVybmVkIE15IFByb2Nlc3MgSW50byBhIFBsdWdpbiIsInBvc3RfaWQiOjQ0NjIsInBvc3RfdHlwZSI6InBvc3QiLCJ1cmwiOiJodHRwczovL2V2ZXJ5LnRvL3BvZGNhc3QiLCJwb3NpdGlvbiI6MTZ9 to talk about how we use AI in editorial work. In the weeks that follow, Laura will report on how professional writers are using AI, Mike Taylor https://every.to/emails/click/1eb47536f45a3508ca723b5b2cb780e942839f966e324ef3162cd49469aec49f/eyJzdWJqZWN0IjoiQ29tcG91bmQgV3JpdGluZzogSG93IEkgVHVybmVkIE15IFByb2Nlc3MgSW50byBhIFBsdWdpbiIsInBvc3RfaWQiOjQ0NjIsInBvc3RfdHlwZSI6InBvc3QiLCJ1cmwiOiJodHRwczovL2V2ZXJ5LnRvL0BtaWtlXzIxMTQiLCJwb3NpdGlvbiI6MTd9 will share his own process, and we’ll close it out with a live write-along.—Kate Lee https://every.to/emails/click/1eb47536f45a3508ca723b5b2cb780e942839f966e3

----------
howdy, it’s Barsee again.

happy wednesday, AI family, and welcome back to AI Valley.

**here are the biggest things worth knowing today:**

* Anthropic released Claude Fable 5.1 and Mythos 5.1

* World Labs has a new world model called Atlas

* Meta has a new real-time speech model

* Plus trending AI tools, posts, and resources

Let’s _dive_ into the Valley of AI…


----------

----------
#### **WISPR FLOW**

## [Walk-and-think (capture ideas on the move)](https://ref.wisprflow.ai/aivalley)

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/ab7bd294-8dd6-42a4-b0ed-7ad980fa70ca/Paid_Media_Newsletter_Image__6___1_.png?t=1788356597)

Caption: Courtesy: Wispr Flow

Some problems don't solve themselves at a keyboard. Flow is perfect for walks: talk through the idea, the structure, the tradeoffs—then get back a clean draft you can paste into your doc or AI tool. It's like having a writing assistant that keeps up with your brain in motion.

[Try Flow Free](https://ref.wisprflow.ai/aivalley)

~_*This is sponsored_~


----------

----------
#### **THROUGH THE VALLEY**

Youtube: Introducing Claude Fable 5.1 (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ROF2Nv_KjOM)

**1/ Anthropic released Claude Fable 5.1 and Mythos 5.1** - they’re actually the [same underlying model](https://www.anthropic.com/claude-fable-and-mythos-5-1), but Fable is available to everyone while Mythos has fewer safeguards for cybersecurity and biology and is only available to vetted organizations. ([read the announcement](https://x.com/claudeai/status/2094848572143407483?s=20))

Fable got a pretty big science/coding bump. It scored 52.6% on Terminal-Bench-Science vs 24.7% for Fable 5, and Anthropic says Mythos is even better at some of the harder research stuff. It designed protein binders with a ~50% hit rate across 12 targets and sped up GPU kernels for biology models by up to 2.5x.

Pricing is still $10/$50 per million input/output tokens, but cache reads are 75% cheaper. Anthropic says that makes typical workloads ~25% cheaper and highly agentic ones up to ~45% cheaper.

**Some fun Fable stuff already:**

* [COLD WATCH](https://cold-watch-game.netlify.app/?utm_source=chatgpt.com) is Ethan Mollick’s retro space-survival game built with Fable 5.1. A pretty fun way to see what a long-running coding agent can actually build.

* [Cat Doom](https://cat-doom.com/) is exactly what it sounds like... a Doom-style FPS with cats. Fable 5.1 built the thing live on stream.

**2/ World Labs has a new world model called Atlas** - it can take images, video and camera movements and turn them into a [3D world](https://www.worldlabs.ai/blog/atlas) you can move around in. You can basically give it a few photos, tell the camera where to go and generate new image/video frames from that exact viewpoint. ([see the example here](https://x.com/davidpantera_/status/2094841083805266401?s=20)) ([another one here](https://x.com/rehan_shei/status/2094955712606593294?s=20))

[They showed](https://x.com/theworldlabs/status/2094839756329041984?s=20) it generating a 1-minute 1440p video from seven reference images, and it can reconstruct [explicit 3D](https://x.com/tamrrat/status/2094848708944724325?s=20) from just one or a few images. More images = less guessing about what the world actually looks like.

The robotics use case is pretty cool too. Atlas can take a few photos of a real space and simulate what a robot’s cameras/depth sensors would see while moving through it. So instead of scanning every training environment with expensive equipment, you could potentially just take some photos and generate the rest.

It’s all one model, trained from scratch, that mixes ideas from LLMs and video models. World Labs says Atlas can perceive, generate and reason about both virtual + physical worlds.

Early access is coming in the next few weeks. ([read the blog here](https://www.worldlabs.ai/blog/atlas))

**3/ Meta has a new real-time speech model** - [Muse Voice Transcribe](https://research.meta.ai/blog/introducing-muse-voice-transcribe) is Meta’s first real-time audio perception model. It does speech-to-text, figures out who’s speaking and knows when someone has stopped talking, all in one model.

The clever bit is it decides how long to listen before writing each word. Meta says this gets it pretty close to the sweet spot between speed and accuracy.

It’s trained across 70+ languages, can handle people switching languages mid-sentence and apparently hour-long conversations with 20+ speakers. And it costs something like $3 per 1,000 voice minutes.

It’s already being used for dictation in Meta’s desktop app and voice input in Muse Code. Live on the API now too. ([read the announcement by Zuck](https://x.com/finkd/status/2094836602681938385?s=20))


--------------------
# TRENDING TOOLS


--------------------
* [Orbis 1.0](https://x.com/viskoai/status/2094817592754291173?s=20) - create living worlds and stream them in real time, with persistent memory, interactivity, and physics-grounded generation of unbounded length

* [Atlas](https://x.com/theworldlabs/status/2094839756329041984?s=20) - the world's first multimodal world model that generates image and video frames with pixel-perfect camera control and reconstructs them in 3D

* [Claude Fable 5.1](https://www.anthropic.com/claude-fable-and-mythos-5-1) - Anthropic’s new top-ranked model upgrade

* [Dyson](https://x.com/Polymarket/status/2094848260150374768?s=20) - launches a $499 AI toothbrush with a built-in camera that identifies gaps between teeth & automatically squirts them with mouthrinse

* [Perplexity hybrid](https://x.com/AravSrinivas/status/2094803607560585411?s=20) - this will allow Computer to orchestrate local models that can run locally on Mac, particularly for agent steps involving sensitive and private files

* [Caddi](https://www.trycaddi.com/?utm_campaign=openai-cuts-cursor-access-following-spacex-buyout&utm_medium=referral&utm_source=aibreakfast.beehiiv.com) - builds AI agents by recording narrated screenshares to automate repetitive back-office work across your existing software

* [Google Pics](https://x.com/GoogleWorkspace/status/2094818432973725961?s=20) - lets you edit individual objects, refine or translate text, and collaborate with your team


----------

----------
# WHAT I'M CONSUMING


--------------------
* OpenAI prepares to release [Astra](https://www.wired.com/story/openai-astra-first-ai-model-with-critical-cyber-abilities) with "critical" cyber capabilities** **to answer Anthropic’s Mythos

* The world's first multimodal [world model](https://x.com/theworldlabs/status/2094839756329041984?s=20) that generates image and video frames with pixel-perfect camera control and reconstructs them in 3D

* Anthropic made an evil model. Of course I have to do a [video](https://x.com/theo/status/2094723660204695749?s=20)

* Nobody is [talking seriously](https://x.com/giovannicatt3/status/2094815425972539565) about AI demand

* Things are now happening [much faster](https://x.com/AISafetyMemes/status/2094980066539344280?s=20) than AI 2027


----------

VIBE CHECK: FABLE 5.1—ANTHROPIC IS SO BACK (AGAIN) https://every.


OUR TESTS SHOW WHERE IT REPLACES FABLE AND OPUS—AND WHERE WE’RE KEEPING THE ALTERNATIVES https://every.

by Katie Parrott https://every.to/emails/click/1eb47536f45a3508ca723b5b2cb780e942839f966e324ef3162cd49469aec49f/eyJzdWJqZWN0IjoiVmliZSBDaGVjazogRmFibGUgNS4x4oCUQW50aHJvcGljIElzIFNvIEJhY2sgKEFnYWluKSIsInBvc3RfaWQiOjQ0NTQsInBvc3RfdHlwZSI6InByb21vIiwidXJsIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly9ldmVyeS50by9Aa2F0aWUucGFycm90dDEyIiwicG9zaXRpb24iOjR9 and Dan Shipper https://every.to/emails/click/1eb47536f45a3508ca723b5b2cb780e942839f966e324ef3162cd49469aec49f/eyJzdWJqZWN0IjoiVmliZSBDaGVjazogRmFibGUgNS4x4oCUQW50aHJvcGljIElzIFNvIEJhY2sgKEFnYWluKSIsInBvc3RfaWQiOjQ0NTQsInBvc3RfdHlwZSI6InByb21vIiwidXJsIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly9ldmVyeS50by9AZGFuc2hpcHBlciIsInBvc2l0aW9uIjo1fQ==

This is a free preview of a subscribers-only post.

Anthropic is so back.

The company just released Fable 5.1, the successor to the model we called the best coder in the world, Fable 5 https://every..

The original Fable was easier to admire than to use. It could take on enormous coding jobs, but slow replies and hard-to-follow explanations made it frustrating when you wanted to talk through an idea or revise a draft.

Anthropic’s new Fable 5.1 brings that coding ability into a model we want to work alongside. It’s faster, writes more clearly, and argues less when we ask it to change course. After a summer that sent much of Every’s team toward ChatGPT and Codex, we’re bringing work back to Claude.

But enthusiasm hasn’t made it our choice for everything. Fable 5.1 still overruns briefs, can invent quotations, and sometimes keeps working when asked to stop. Easier to use doesn’t mean ready to leave unchecked.

Our full Vibe Check https://every. gets into:

newsletters.title: What We Learned From 15 Hours of Anthropic Certification Training
newsletters.content:
AI education is still in its early days. A shared set of definitions is key to what comes next.  ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌

WHAT WE LEARNED FROM 15 HOURS OF ANTHROPIC CERTIFICATION TRAINING https://every.


AI EDUCATION IS STILL IN ITS EARLY DAYS. A SHARED SET OF DEFINITIONS IS KEY TO WHAT COMES NEXT. https://every.

by Natalia Quintero https://every.

Midjourney/Every illlustration.

Was this newsletter forwarded to you? Sign up https://every.to/emails/click/1eb47536f45a3508ca723b5b2cb780e942839f966e324ef3162cd49469aec49f/eyJzdWJqZWN0IjoiV2hhdCBXZSBMZWFybmVkIEZyb20gMTUgSG91cnMgb2YgQW50aHJvcGljIENlcnRpZmljYXRpb24gVHJhaW5pbmciLCJwb3N0X2lkIjo0NDU2LCJwb3N0X3R5cGUiOiJwb3N0IiwidXJsIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly9ldmVyeS50by9hY2NvdW50IiwicG9zaXRpb24iOjR9 to get it in your inbox.



----------------------------------------



Fifteen years ago, I took my first online course on edX, a learning provider founded by MIT and Harvard. At the time, edX was cutting edge and I binge-watched a ton of courses. (I still love and recommend Michael Sandel’s course Justice, but that’s beside the point.)

I found myself recalling that time when I took four courses earlier this summer to earn our team Anthropic certification https://every.. After working closely with the Anthropic team for more than a year as alpha testers of unreleased models, we wanted to take our partnership farther. I went into the certification process curious about what level of instruction they’d provide and how they’d define their own tools. What I came away with was new insight into the state of AI development and industry standards right now.

AI development is still moving at a breakneck pace, but new releases no longer upend our work the way they used to. Anthropic’s Opus 4.5 and OpenAI’s GPT-5.5 marked a turning point as the models could reliably perform the tasks we provide, giving each subsequent release a dependable base to build on. The fact that Anthropic can even release a training course for its foundational tools like Claude Code and agent skills is a milestone for the AI era. (This time last year, I was constantly reworking the curriculum for our training sessions every three to six weeks when a new, more capable model came out.)

More stable models have allowed people to build AI workflows around their individual roles and careers. Anthropic’s training takes the opposite tack—it teaches foundational concepts. But the greatest value of these courses may not be sparking new ideas for the tools we use day to day. Instead, they offer an opportunity for the industry to align around terms and definitions—a heavy lift on its own.


SHARED REFERENCE POINTS, NOT PLAYBOOKS

To become Anthropic certified, companies are required to take four courses: Introduction to Agent Skills, Building with Claude API, Introduction to Model Context Protocol (MCP), and Claude Code in Action. The full course load takes roughly 10 to 15 hours per person.

Each online training involves reading through text-based how-tos interspersed with short videos and sample exercises, much like the many online courses I’ve taken previously—including in those edX days.

None of the four courses delivers a playbook for transforming workflows with AI—mapping workflows, identifying tasks ripe to streamline with AI, and codifying tasks into skills. Instead, they offer common definitions: This is what Anthropic says a skill is; this is what an MCP is; this is how an API works.

Definitions may seem like a starting bid for a training, but they are critical when you’re creating the foundation for tools that you want hundreds of millions of people to use, which Anthropic is—this certification is literally AI 101.

If Anthropic’s definition of an MCP diverges from an individual company’s, that difference could hurt effective AI implementation. Having a shared language is important when we’re still figuring out AI adoption as an industry.

I felt the benefit myself. I’m not often building MCPs, so despite how often we use them at Every, my understanding only clicked into place when the course walked through the endpoints and logic underneath them.

The training also gave our team a shared reference point. Getting roughly a third of the company to take this course catalyzed a conversation internally about how we learn. While the training is good, the Every team consensus is that Anthropic’s documentation https://every., a publicly available collection of guides and resources for common use cases, is much better. If you really want to understand how Claude works, skip the videos—the documentation is the gold standard.


ONE-SIZE-FITS-ALL TRAINING FOR A RAPIDLY SPECIALIZING FIELD

While the pace of change at the model level has slowed, the user experience of the software around AI models is changing faster than ever. Unfortunately, the courses reflected that.

The Building with Claude API course uses a Sonnet model that’s no longer available in the API, and the MCP course doesn’t mention Anthropic’s own MCP builder skill. I don’t mean that as a criticism of Anthropic. It’s a symptom of how fast things are changing, and an occupational hazard when trying to capture a still-developing process for educational purposes.

The courses also don’t take your role or experience level into account, or assess what you already know before moving into the material. Whether you’re a CFO, an engineer, or an intern, your experience working through certification is identical. This feels like a missed opportunity when AI is already very good a

howdy, it’s Barsee again.

happy monday, AI family, and welcome back to AI Valley.

**here are the biggest things worth knowing today:**

* AI video is now fast enough to make infinite livestreams

* John Ternus is taking over Apple, and AI is the big test

* Anthropic wants AI agents to operate real-world hardware

* Plus trending AI tools, posts, and resources

Let’s _dive_ into the Valley of AI…


----------

----------
#### **MOONSHOTS LIVE**

## [$2M to founders who used AI on a problem people have](https://moonshots.com/landing/ai-valley?utm_source=ai-valley&utm_medium=newsletter&utm_campaign=mslive25&utm_content=2026-08-31)

Caption: _Courtesy: Moonshots Live_

Most of the futures we get shown are the ones falling apart. That is a failure of imagination with real consequences, because the futures we picture are the ones we end up building. So we put $5.5M behind the other kind.

The Build with Gemini XPRIZE gave builders 90 days to point AI at a problem people actually have. $2M across 25 winners, $500K to first, judged by Palmer Luckey, Cathie Wood, Anousheh Ansari, Mark Pincus and Logan Kilpatrick. Revenue was the proof it worked, not the point.

The same night a film gets greenlit for a $2.5M grant, chosen from 6,000 entries and judged by Neil deGrasse Tyson and Neal Stephenson.

More than 30,000 people competed. Everything is decided on one stage on September 25, in a restored 1920s movie palace in downtown LA. Nothing pre-recorded. 1,500 seats.

_[Claim your seats](https://moonshots.com/landing/ai-valley?utm_source=ai-valley&utm_medium=newsletter&utm_campaign=mslive25&utm_content=2026-08-31)_

~_*This is sponsored_~


----------

----------
#### **THROUGH THE VALLEY**

Tweet:  (https://twitter.com/rehan_shei/status/2093528415576211819?s=20)

**1/ AI video is now fast enough to make infinite livestreams** - [fal’s H3 Max](https://fal.ai/minimax-h3-max) can generate 15 seconds of video in roughly 9 seconds, which is faster than the video can play. Rehan Sheikh [hooked it up to a livestream](https://x.com/rehan_shei/status/2093528415576211819?s=20) and made an “infinite interdimensional cable” where the AI just keeps generating the next scene.

Then Pieter Levels built [Infinite Slop](https://infiniteslop.ai/) where you can type something into the chat and AI generates it into the next part of the stream. 37,000 people watched on day one.

The interesting bit is that video can now be generated _while_ you’re watching it. Instead of making a finished piece of media and then distributing it, the media itself can keep changing based on what the audience does. You make the movie, song or video first, then people watch it. Now the thing itself can keep generating, responding and changing based on the audience.

Feels like we’re getting the first glimpse of media becoming less like a file and more like a living thing.

**2/ John Ternus is taking over Apple, and AI is the big test** - Ternus becomes CEO tomorrow, [taking over from Tim Cook](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-08-30/apple-s-new-ceo-john-ternus-takes-reins-from-tim-cook-focusing-on-ai?accessToken=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJzb3VyY2UiOiJTdWJzY3JpYmVyR2lmdGVkQXJ0aWNsZSIsImlhdCI6MTc4ODE0ODY2NSwiZXhwIjoxNzg4NzUzNDY1LCJhcnRpY2xlSWQiOiJUS0xQMDFLSUpIOEswMCIsImJjb25uZWN0SWQiOiJCMzZENUE5QzIxMDQ0NjU4OTFBMTc1MTVDRDNBQkZFNiJ9.9bcyLTjfplSATZnfIn1JK08SA39tqdvrEz2bMOZOREw&utm_source=tldrnewsletter&leadSource=article-gifting) after 15 years. Cook isn’t really going anywhere though. He’ll stay as executive chairman and keep handling relationships with Trump and China while Ternus gets to deal with the fun stuff.

He’s coming in with a pretty wild product roadmap: a foldable iPhone, a new home display, smart glasses, camera-equipped AirPods and more. A lot of it depends on Apple finally getting its AI stuff working properly.

Apple has fallen behind in AI, so the big test is the new Siri. Apple is using Google’s Gemini as the foundation after struggling with its own models, and the new version is supposed to finally make Siri actually useful.

Ternus also wants to use AI internally to speed up product development and testing. So yeah, the next few years at Apple are going to be pretty interesting.

**3/ Anthropic wants AI agents to operate real-world hardware** - Anthropic and HHMI Janelia released a research preview of the [Model Hardware Standard](https://www.anthropic.com/news/model-hardware-standard-research-preview), a common interface that lets AI agents work with things like microscopes, lab robots and quantum equipment.

The coolest example is QuEra. Claude used MHS to build a laser recovery script that successfully restored the laser lock in 695 of 700 tests, or 99.3%. The script then runs without Claude needing to stay in the loop.

MHS is basically trying to do for physical hardware what APIs did for software. Instead of building a custom integration for every machine, agents get a standard way to discover and control them.

Still early, and Claude needs human oversight for physical problems. But this feels like an important step toward agents that can actually _do_ things in the real world.

Youtube: AI models can now help run physical science experiments (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=P1zBiAQU1IA)


----------

----------
# TRENDING TOOLS


--------------------
* [Diffusion Studio](https://x.com/konstipaulus/status/2093344586315747706/video/1) - an open-source video editor that turns every edit into code

* [Motion](https://x.com/motion_so/status/2094123213735305359?s=20) - paste your website URL and turn it into a launch video with motion graphics, voiceover, music, and captions

* [Radar](https://radar.particle.pro/) - a search engine for podcasts that helps you find every episode mentioning a person, company, topic, or keyword

* [H3 Max](https://fal.ai/models/minimax/h3-max/text-to-video) - Fal’s top-ranked post-trained video model, optimized for speed and quality

* [Expert Intelligence](https://x.com/i/trending/2093095464996626462) - Google launches the ability to integrate ebooks into Gemini Notebook

* [LLM Cliché Highlighter](https://tools.simonwillison.net/llm-cliche-highlighter) - scan pasted text or a URL for common AI-writing tells and see exactly which patterns were detected

* [OpenClaw 2.0](https://openclaw.ai/blog/openclaw-2-accidentally/) - its biggest update yet, built by 933 contributors. Messaging, memory, skills, and automations have all been upgraded

* [Hy4 Preview](https://hy.tencent.ai/research/hy4-preview) - Tencent’s new 770-billion-parameter flagship model with 49 billion active parameters and a 1-million-token context window

* [Claude Cowork](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=63GVebZvqok) - the desktop app now includes a built-in browser that lets Claude navigate websites
